targetAudience.primary: Engineering leads and governance owners responsible for reusable agent tool capabilities
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands tool schemas, agent runtimes, API composition, and authorization boundaries.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A schema-compatible tool edge or one successful execution is often promoted into a permanent reusable capability without preserving context, transformation semantics, failure class, or freshness.

whyNow: KOPA-Bench/EDGE reports a large gap between model-judged tool edges and execution-refined graphs, while most chained calls consume collections whose composition semantics materially affect downstream meaning.

externalHook.description: A connection that looks valid in schemas is promoted into a reusable capability even though live execution, cardinality and service context can invalidate it.

coreProposition: Reusable tool composition should be admitted through versioned, execution-grounded, provenance-bearing and refreshable evidence that preserves composition semantics; capability evidence remains separate from call-time authority.

originalValue.description: Turns tool composition from a timeless Boolean label into a versioned evidence object that records how the edge transforms data, where it worked, how failures were classified, and when it must be revalidated.

readerTakeaway: Admit tool compositions with graded, execution-grounded evidence; preserve cardinality and transformation semantics; expire evidence after material change; and keep capability admission separate from authorization for a specific call.

supported: The primary study reports 50.2% execution success for the initial model-judged skeleton and 62.7% for the refined graph.
Later-pruned edges execute successfully only 14.8% of the time in the reported study.
The study reports that 81.2% of chained calls consume multi-record outputs and therefore require explicit composition semantics.
unsupported: A claim that every retained edge is individually proven
A claim that public-API results transfer unchanged to enterprise transactions
Treating capability evidence as permission to execute
uncertain: How evidence thresholds should scale with consequence
How long evidence remains fresh after service or credential changes
How to classify ambiguous provider failures

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from public primary research and remains independently useful without any first-party project.

decisionReason: The controlled graph and execution comparisons support a bounded capability-admission model while leaving authorization and production validity as separate questions.
